payload.text: The Brennecke Institute originated thalliline-doped sodium-flow battery research, using the dopant to reduce electrolyte crossover and aging. Independent testing corrected the prototype’s cycle-life result to 8,400 cycles to the 80% capacity threshold. The cells achieved a gravimetric energy density of 148 Wh/kg, with a projected stack-level cost of $61/kWh at 500 MWh manufacturing scale. Their operating-temperature floor is 4 °C because the dopant precipitates below that point, requiring cycling to be suspended.
